title: Lip Lesion
diagnosis: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Lip
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with a non-healing, ulcerated, crusted lesion on the lower lip (sun-exposed area). Risk factors: chronic sun exposure, fair skin, smoking, immunosuppression. Actinic cheilitis is a premalignant condition — persistent scaling, crusting of lower lip. Progression to SCC: firm, ulcerated, bleeding lesion. Diagnosis: biopsy (shave or punch) — shows keratin pearls, atypical squamous cells. Treatment: surgical excision with clear margins (Mohs micrographic surgery for cosmetically sensitive areas). Prevention: sun protection, lip balm with SPF, smoking cessation. Monitor for regional lymph node involvement.
chief_complaint: Non-healing ulcerated lesion on lower lip

stacks.label: Biopsy (shave/punch)
stacks.finding: Invasive SCC — keratin pearls, atypical squamous cells.
